sentences.text: The name Parasuchus combines Greek words meaning 'beside' and 'Sobek,' the Egyptian crocodile god.
The species name hislopi honors Hislop, who drew attention to the red clay deposits near Maleri village where the fossils were found.
Two nearly complete skeletons of Parasuchus were found together, each roughly 8 feet in length.
This predator possessed a powerful bite, estimated at 450 newtons at the front of the jaw and 1,958 newtons at the back.
Richard Lydekker formally described and named Parasuchus hislopi in 1885 and proposed the family name Parasuchidae.
The original nondiagnostic holotype was replaced by a neotype designated in 2001 following an application by Sankar Chatterjee.
Two complete, articulated skeletons with complete skulls were found near the Mutapyram village in the Adilabad district.
Parasuchus belongs to the family Parasuchidae.
A 2016 study placed Parasuchus hislopi within the same evolutionary group as the species Paleorhinus bransoni and Paleorhinus angustifrons.
Some researchers consider Parasuchus to be a senior synonym of the genus Paleorhinus, meaning species formerly in Paleorhinus are now placed in Parasuchus.
Parasuchus lived during the Late Triassic period, specifically from the late Carnian to early Norian stages, in India.
It is debated whether Parasuchus should be treated as a separate genus or synonymized with the genus Paleorhinus.
